claims: Some vaccines require multiple doses over several weeks to become effective.
According to CDC recommendations, common travel vaccines include routine vaccines such as COVID-19, Flu, MMR (Measles-Mumps-Rubella), Tdap (Tetanus-Diphtheria-Pertussis), and Varicella (Chickenpox).
CDC recommends Hepatitis A vaccine for most travelers to countries with intermediate or high-risk food/water sources.
CDC recommends Typhoid vaccine for travelers visiting smaller cities, villages, or rural areas, particularly if visiting developing countries.
Yellow Fever vaccine is required for entry into certain countries in Africa and South America.
Yellow Fever vaccine must be administered at an authorized clinic.
CDC recommends Japanese Encephalitis vaccine for long-term stays or travel to rural areas in Asia.
CDC recommends Rabies vaccine for travelers visiting areas with high risk, or those spending long periods abroad, doing outdoor activities, or working with animals.
CDC recommends Meningococcal (ACWY) vaccine for travel to specific areas such as the "meningitis belt" in Africa or for the Hajj pilgrimage.
The "yellow card" is the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP).
The "yellow card" (ICVP) is needed if the yellow fever vaccine was received.
Travel vaccines are available at specialized travel clinics.
Travel vaccines are available at local health departments.
Travel vaccines are available at some pharmacies like CVS or Walgreens.
The CDC Travelers' Health website lists specific vaccine requirements and recommendations by destination.
